sources.entry: Ruby.app - macOS app that contains a full Ruby installation (for use with Ruby/Gosu).

summary.one_liner: Ruby.app is a macOS application wrapper that bundles a full universal MRI Ruby installation so Ruby apps and Ruby/Gosu games can be shipped as a standalone .app.
summary.what_it_does: The repository provides a Ruby.app bundle containing a self-contained, universal (Intel and ARM) MRI/C Ruby installation. The user places a main.rb file in Ruby.app/Contents/Resources/ to start their game or application. The README says it has so far only been used for Ruby/Gosu games but could be adapted to other toolkits. The build process uses rvm on an Intel Mac and an ARM Mac, with a Rakefile that installs Ruby and gems, and then merges the binaries into a UniversalRuby folder. The README also says Ruby versions and gems can be set in the Rakefile.
use_cases: Package a Ruby/Gosu game as a macOS app
Ship a Ruby application without requiring users to install Ruby
Bundle a universal Ruby runtime for Intel and Apple Silicon Macs
Avoid depending on the deprecated system Ruby on macOS
Wrap a Ruby script in a double-clickable macOS application
how_to_run: Optional: update the Rakefile with the desired Ruby version and gems
Install rvm on one Intel Mac and one ARM Mac
Run rake on the Intel Mac to install Ruby and gems via rvm and copy them into the UniversalRuby folder
AirDrop the UniversalRuby folder to the ARM Mac
Run rake on the ARM Mac to build and merge ARM binaries into the UniversalRuby folder
notable: Full universal Ruby installation bundled inside the .app, so users don't need Ruby installed
Built to handle C extensions common in Ruby/Gosu games
Build requires one Intel Mac and one ARM Mac to produce universal binaries
Free and MIT-licensed, positioned as an alternative to RubyMotion and Platypus
caveats: Build requires both an Intel Mac and an ARM Mac plus rvm, which is a heavy setup
Known issue: OpenSSL and YAML extensions have unportable dependencies on /opt/homebrew (the README text is cut off here)
Ruby installation licensing is separate; users must check Ruby and standard library licenses
